correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all definitions and normalizations. On each nonzero character the Laplacian eigenvalue is exactly 4 sin^2(pi k/N), so the Riesz multiplier is i exp(pi i k/N). Exact geometric and sine sums give the two kernels, and direct parity substitution gives the block identity. The square identity is frequencywise exact. Finite-group row and column sums give sharp endpoint norms, with explicit attaining data. The asymptotic uses a smooth singularity subtraction and Euler--Maclaurin; computations only replay these formulas.

value.rationale: This is not an arbitrary finite invariant. It gives an exact operator-theoretic bridge between two canonical discrete singular transforms: the cycle graph Riesz transform is a square root of a translated negative identity on mean-zero data, and the doubled cyclic Hilbert transform is exactly its parity block extension. The bridge yields a closed kernel, sharp endpoints, and parity-dependent finite-size behavior and can be reused when transferring questions between graph and Fourier singular transforms.
